value.body: The Agricultural Scientists Recruitment Board (ASRB) recruits scientists for the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) through the Agricultural Research Service (ARS) exam. Selected candidates join as Scientist at an ICAR institute and work on research, extension and training — in veterinary and animal sciences as well as crops, fisheries and other fields.

items.label: Minimum qualification
items.value: Master’s degree in a relevant discipline
items.note: A BVSc & AH alone is not enough

items.label: ARS age limit
items.note: Relaxations for reserved categories and PhD holders

items.label: Stages
items.note: Prelims is combined with NET, SMS and STO

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Complete a master's degree (for example an MVSc) in a discipline listed in the ASRB notification. ASRB holds a combined preliminary exam for NET, ARS, SMS and STO; ARS candidates who clear it take a descriptive mains exam and an interview. Discipline-wise qualifications and age limits are in each year's notification.

value.title: At a glance
items: Vacancies are discipline-specific, so a given subject may have only a few posts in a year.
The same prelims also offers ASRB NET, used for lecturer / assistant professor eligibility in agricultural universities.
Postings can be at research stations in remote areas.
A PhD is not required to apply but gives age relaxation and supports later career growth.
